name: Monomem
description: Self-hosted shared memory for AI coding agents: one SQLite file on the user's machine, shared by every connected tool. Each note carries a server-stamped writer, version history and undo. Reads and ordinary saves keep Guard's usual handling; deleting, replacing, merging, purging history, changing trust or quarantine, and queueing or approving tasks are gated on review. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Every tool reads or writes only the local SQLite store; nothing is sent off the machine and no model is called. The server binds 127.0.0.1 by default and ships no tunnel.
A default install registers only ten tools (state_*, catch_up and the supersede preview/confirm/undo trio). The rest appear only when MONOMEM_TOOLS opts them in.
written_by is stamped by the server from the authenticated token, never from tool input. Give each agent its own scoped read/write token to tell writers apart.
Every write is linted: likely secrets are refused, and prompt-injection text is quarantined until an admin reviews it. memory_quarantine releases or drops held writes, so it stays on review.
Replacing a note is a two-step preview then confirm, and memory_supersede_undo reverses it. state_delete removes the note text from the database file, so it stays on review.
task_put can queue a command task for the separately run, unpublished command runner, and task_approve lets it run; both stay on review.
This entry matches npx monomem mcp (npx -y monomem@1.0.4 mcp as written by monomem setup). A node <path>/cli.js mcp launch, or cmd /c npx on Windows, keeps Guard's normal handling.
